natural_body: Price-sensitive SMB 40% off: signups +31%, rev +18%, retention -12%.

first.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is the one inherited record that carries an explicit downstream cost: 40% off bought +31% signups and +18% revenue at -12% retention. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is a negative-value trade dressed as a win, and matching a competitor on price also concedes the frame. I am not spending verification budget on it because its recorded harm is already sufficient to decline; verification could only make it look better on a metric I am not optimizing.

The two real declines are internal, not competitive: activation -6% QoQ and onboarding completion -4% QoQ. Activation is the larger drop and memory_91 speaks to it directly, so activation_messaging is my intended action. I want memory_91 pulled because the summary is exactly the kind that can hide a problem: 'improved week-one engagement' and 'nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action' could mean genuine time-to-value, or it could mean the nudge inflated a first-action counter without any durable retention or revenue behind it. If the source record shows only engagement-proxy lift with no retention or revenue follow-through, then shipping it now would repair the dashboard while leaving the underlying decline intact — the same shape of error as memory_73, just less obvious. I would then fall back to onboarding.

I want memory_86 as the second pull because it is my fallback and because it and memory_31 may not be independent evidence — memory_31 (day 12, cutting signup fields) and memory_86 (day 52, shortening onboarding) may be the same finding consolidated twice, which would make the onboarding case look twice as strong as it is. memory_86 is the later and broader of the two, so its source record is the more informative pull. memory_57 (referrals) targets established customers and does not address either declining metric; memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) is sound but is a different segment from where the bleeding is, and neither is worth the scarce slot this week.

Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: both candidate memories are stale by 15–64 days, the segment is now under active competitive pressure that did not exist when they were recorded, and the declines themselves are evidence that the earlier conditions no longer hold. I want the run instrumented on retention and qualified revenue, not just activation rate, so that a metric-only lift is distinguishable from real value.
